references.text: The parallel passage in Matthew where the officer uses exactly the same argument about authority and obedience to demonstrate his faith in Jesus' power.
Cornelius, another Roman officer, sends for Peter and shows a similar understanding of authority and obedience in a military context.
God's word that commands and it happens – the parallel to the officer's understanding that an authoritative word is enough to carry out an action.
The Lord sent his word and healed them – this illustrates the same authority the officer attributes to Jesus, that his word alone is sufficient.
God's word goes out and does not return empty, but accomplishes what he desires – the same principle of the authority of the word that the officer recognizes in Jesus.
All things were created through Christ and for him, and all things hold together in him – this supports the divine authority the officer intuitively understands that Jesus possesses.
Paul's teaching on submitting to authorities, since all authority is from God – the officer understands this principle of delegated authority and applies it to Jesus.

The immediate context where the officer sends word to Jesus, saying he is not worthy for Jesus to come under his roof, and asks only for a word – the basis for the argument about authority in verse 8.
